name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=render, descriptor=recruitment_select_screen). Composes one frame of the recruitment / chapter-branch party-select screen (10-wide portrait grid + counter digits + cursor highlight + cursor-char stat panel) into the shared composed-target surface. Name accurately reflects the purpose; no address residue.
purpose: Compose one frame of the recruitment / chapter-branch party-select screen into the shared 64000-byte composed-target working surface (caller later memmoves it to VGA 0xA0000).
logic_summary: void __cdecl, 4 stack params, Watcom __CHK(0x28) stack-probe prologue (compiler-injected, omitted in src). Steps: (1) memmove(surface, panel_buf, 64000) restores the pre-built base panel. (2) Render top 'max' digits (value=max_chars) at surface+0x2BFD via fd2_render_decimal_number_to_buffer (stride 0x140, color 0x1F, 2 digits). (3) fd2_count_selected_chars(sel_state) called twice -- only the 2nd return is kept (1st discarded; preserved as-is from the original). (4) Render bottom 'remaining' digits (value=max_chars-count) at surface+0x5B7D (color 0x2A, 2 digits). (5) fd2_tick_chapter_palette_animation(), read data_fd2_graphics_chapter_ambient_palette_anim_idx, collapse idx 3->1 (4 phases map to 3 frame slots). (6) fd2_render_full_char_stat_panel(cursor_idx+1, surface) draws the cursor char stat panel. (7) Cursor highlight blit: src = runtime_battle_state + *(int*)(runtime_battle_state+6); dst cell uses a 10-wide grid (col 0x1C px, row 0x1E px, base y 0x68 rows): surface + (cursor%10)*0x1C+0x17 + ((cursor/10)*0x1E+0x68)*0x140, via fd2_tile_blit_24x24_passthrough. (8) For iter in [0, menu_party_member_count - 1): char_off uses same 10-wide grid (base y 100 rows); rle_stream = cache + cache[(iter*0xC + palette_idx + 0xC)*4] (0xC=12 four-byte sprite-offset entries per char; +0xC skips the first entry block = the always-present lord/leader, matching the caller cursor-wrap bounds of member_count-1/-2/-11). sel_state[iter]==0 -> fd2_tile_blit_24x24_dimmed_grayscale at the cell (un-picked, grayed); else fd2_tile_blit_24x24_passthrough at cell+0x3C0 (3 rows lower = 'pressed' effect). No return. Decompilation matches src body exactly.
signature: void __cdecl fd2_render_recruitment_select_screen(uint32 panel_buf, uint32 max_chars, uint32 sel_state, uint32 cursor_idx)

params.name: panel_buf
params.semantics: Linear address of the pre-built base panel backup buffer (caller's malloc'd pvVar2 with header banner + grid frame already blitted in). memmove'd into the working surface at the top of every frame to restore the base.
params.reason: Accurately names the base-panel backup buffer used as the per-frame restore source; no address residue.
params.ghidra_param_note: Ghidra decompiler shows this param as param_1; src naming is correct.

params.name: max_chars
params.semantics: Recruit cap for this chapter: 0x0F normally, 0x13 when current_chapter_id > 0x1A. Drives the top 'max' digit display and the 'remaining' = max_chars - count digit display.
params.reason: Accurate recruit-cap name; matches both callers; no address residue.
params.ghidra_param_note: Ghidra decompiler shows this param as param_2; src naming is correct.

params.name: sel_state
params.semantics: Pointer (as uint32) to the selection_state byte array (caller's 32-byte local, first 30 used): byte[i]==1 means slot i is picked (drawn pressed via passthrough), ==0 means not picked (drawn dimmed grayscale). Also passed to fd2_count_selected_chars.
params.reason: Accurate selection-state name; matches the caller's selection_state local and fd2_count_selected_chars usage; no address residue.
params.ghidra_param_note: Ghidra decompiler shows this param as param_3; src naming is correct.

params.name: cursor_idx
params.semantics: Current cursor grid slot index (integer). Passed by both callers as an int (initial render passes 0; re-renders pass the running cursor_idx). Used as an integer: cursor_idx+1 for the stat-panel call, and cursor_idx%10 / cursor_idx/10 for the 10-wide highlight cell.
params.reason: Accurately names the integer cursor index; body uses it purely as an int (no dereference); no address residue.
params.ghidra_param_note: Ghidra decompiler mis-names this param 'backup_buf' (declared uint*) -- a stale decompiler artifact; it is NOT a buffer pointer. The plate comment already documents this ('passed as uint* but used as int integer index'). The Ghidra-side param name backup_buf -> cursor_idx is a candidate Stage-2 Ghidra rename; src is already correct so no proposed change is recorded here.

returns.semantics: No return value (frame composed into the shared surface; caller memmoves surface to VGA 0xA0000). Binary ends in a plain RET; both callers discard.
